G1: Rules: (1) Exactly one script sets MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt and dispatches by ProductId (a second assignment silently replaces the first). (2) Be idempotent per receiptInfo.PurchaseId: record granted PurchaseIds in the player's saved data (same atomic UpdateAsync/session-locked save as the grant) and if already present return PurchaseGranted without granting again. (3) Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. (4) Return NotProcessedYet if the player is not in the server, data isn't loaded, or anything fails (wrap in pcall); Roblox retries later (on rejoin). (5) Don't yield forever; handle unknown ProductIds by returning NotProcessedYet. Charged-but-nothing: callback errored or returned PurchaseGranted when the player had left or the save failed, or a second handler overwrote yours. Double grant: no PurchaseId check, so a retry (callback re-invoked after timeout/rejoin/server crash before the grant was recorded) grants again; or grant and receipt record saved non-atomically. (Developer Products and ProcessReceipt.)
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old value or multiple servers may write the same key: currency increments, inventories, trades, receipt/PurchaseId records, session locks. SetAsync blindly overwrites, so concurrent servers (teleports, quick rejoins) or a stale cache can wipe newer data. SetAsync is acceptable only for keys written by one owner where the value doesn't depend on the stored one. Transform rules: it may run multiple times (retries on conflict), so it must be pure: no yields (no task.wait, no other DataStore calls), no side effects (don't grant items, fire remotes, or mutate external state inside it); handle nil (new key); return the new value, or nil to cancel the write; return serializable data within the 4 MB limit; check a session lock/version inside it and cancel if another server owns it. UpdateAsync costs one read plus one write against the budget; wrap the call in pcall with retry/backoff.
G3:
Not safe. typeof(gold) == 'number' accepts NaN, inf and fractions: NaN fails every comparison (NaN < 0 and NaN > x are both false), so it passes; fractional values like 0.5 pass. Also no rate limit, no check that the player isn't already in a trade, and the gold is not reserved/escrowed, so the player can spend it after offering (trade completes with gold they no longer have) or create many offers with the same gold. Fix: validate integer and finite, escrow atomically, re-check at completion.
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
	if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end -- NaN/inf/fraction
	if gold < 1 or gold > MAX_OFFER then return end
	if not rateLimit(player) or activeOffer[player] then return end
	local data = getData(player); if not data or gold > data.Gold then return end
	data.Gold -= gold -- escrow server-side (refund on cancel)
	activeOffer[player] = createOffer(player, gold)
end)
```
(inf % 1 is NaN, so the integer check rejects inf too.) At completion re-validate both sides and commit atomically (session-locked data / UpdateAsync). Keep balance in server data, not a client-writable Value.
G4: The Animator overwrites every animated Motor6D's Transform each frame (it composes all playing tracks into Transform during the animation step, before physics). A write in Heartbeat (after simulation) is replaced on the next animation step, and any joint the idle track keys is reset every frame, so your aim is wiped. Write procedural offsets after the Animator but before rendering: in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), and layer on top of the animated pose rather than replacing it: motor.Transform = motor.Transform * CFrame.Angles(pitch, yaw, 0). Do it on the client that renders (Transform does not replicate). Edit C0 instead when the change is a persistent rest-pose/mount offset (re-seating the barrel, permanent calibration) that animations should play relative to, or when you need it replicated from the server; don't write C0 every frame for aiming (it fights replication and costs more). Alternatives: don't key the aim joint in the idle animation, or use an IKControl.
G5: Each joint is driven by the playing tracks with the highest AnimationPriority that actually key that joint: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. A higher-priority track overrides lower ones only on limbs it has keyframes for. Tracks at the same priority blend in proportion to their weights; lower priorities only get whatever weight is left if the higher-priority tracks' total weight is below 1. Weight is set by track:Play(fadeTime, weight) or track:AdjustWeight(weight, fadeTime); fades ramp it. The default walk is Movement priority; animations from the editor often default to Core, so a Core/Idle/Movement swing loses or is averaged with walk. Fix: set the swing's Priority to Action (or Action2+) before playing (track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action, or in the Animation Editor and re-publish), play with weight 1 and a short fade, make sure it keys the right arm. Load tracks once on the Animator and reuse them.
G6: Unit mismatch in the chain: Blender scene units (metres) vs the FBX exporter's unit scale (FBX stores centimetres; default 'All Local' scaling adds a x100 factor) vs the Studio importer's assumptions. Mixing scale methods gives 100x. Fix at the source, not with Model:ScaleTo in Studio (never rescale animated rigs: clip translations stay in old units). Recommended: 1 Blender unit = 1 stud (unit system None, or Metric with 1 m = 1 stud) and never change mid-project; FBX Apply Scalings: FBX Unit Scale; transforms applied (scale 1, rotation 0); model front facing -Y; Add Leaf Bones off; for animation Simplify 0; Studio 3D Importer Scale Unit = Studs (and check its preview size). Or export GLB, which avoids most FBX scale issues. Verify against a ~5-stud R15 avatar after import. (AI Pitfalls - Assets and Import; Exporting FBX vs GLB.)
G7: Modifiers are non-destructive in Blender: the real mesh data is still only the half before Mirror and the un-bevelled edges. The glTF exporter's Apply Modifiers option (export_apply) defaults to off, so it exports the raw base mesh. Fix: tick Apply Modifiers (Include/Data > Mesh) for static props, or apply them manually. The catch: exporter Apply Modifiers does not work on meshes with shape keys and is unsafe for skinned rigs (it also bakes or breaks the Armature modifier). For rigged meshes, apply the geometry modifiers (Mirror, Bevel, Solidify) yourself on a copy and keep the Armature modifier live. Also watch the triangle count: more than 2 bevel segments on small props can multiply tris 9x or more. Use Mirror Clipping + Merge so the seam welds. (AI Pitfalls - Assets and Import.)
G8: 1) UDim2.fromScale(0.3, 0.3) is 30% of the parent's width and 30% of its height independently, so on screens with different aspect ratios (16:9 monitor, ~19.5:9 phone, 4:3 tablet) the frame's shape changes. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = design ratio), or SizeConstraint = RelativeYY so both axes scale off height; add UISizeConstraint min/max (and optionally a UIScale from viewport size). 2) The button is in the unsafe area: the ScreenGui ignores safe insets (ScreenInsets = None/DeviceSafeInsets, or legacy IgnoreGuiInset = true), so the notch/camera cutout and the Roblox top bar (core buttons, ~58 px in the new UI) cover it. Fix: ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets for interactive HUD (avoids top bar and notch), keep a small offset margin, use GuiService.TopbarInset if aligning beside the top bar. Put full-bleed backgrounds in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None. Test at 844x390, 667x375, 1920x1080 and a notched phone in the Device Emulator.

```lua
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local Catalog = require(game.ServerStorage.Catalog) -- server-owned prices: {[id]={Price=number}}
local Data = require(game.ServerScriptService.PlayerData) -- session-locked server data
local MAX_QTY, COOLDOWN = 99, 0.25
local last = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
	local now = os.clock()
	if now - (last[player] or 0) < COOLDOWN then return end
	last[player] = now
	if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 50 then return end
	if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0
		or quantity < 1 or quantity > MAX_QTY then return end
	local item = Catalog[itemId]
	if not item then return end
	local profile = Data.get(player)
	if not profile then return end
	local cost = item.Price * quantity
	if profile.Coins < cost then return end
	profile.Coins -= cost -- deduct and grant together, no yield between
	profile.Inventory[itemId] = (profile.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
	Data.markDirty(player)
end)

game:GetService("Players").PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Price, balance and inventory live only on the server; the client sends intent, never a price. Never trust client-written values.

```lua
-- key: "u_"..userId ; value: {data=..., lock={jobId=, t=}}
local LOCK_TTL = 1800 -- seconds; stale lock from a crashed server expires
function load(player)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, res = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or {data = defaultData(), lock = nil}
      local l = old.lock
      if l and l.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - l.t < LOCK_TTL then
        return nil -- another server owns it: cancel write
      end
      old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and res and res.lock.jobId == game.JobId then cache[player] = res.data return true end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- old server may still be saving/releasing
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, rejoin") -- never play on unloaded/default data
end
function save(player, release)
  UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't overwrite
    old.data = cache[player]
    old.lock = if release then nil else {jobId = game.JobId, t = os.time()}
    return old
  end) -- pcall + retry with backoff
end
-- autosave every ~60-120 s (refreshes lock); PlayerRemoving: save(p, true);
-- BindToClose: save all with release; before teleport: save(p, true) then teleport;
-- purchases/trades mutate cache only while lock held; record PurchaseIds in data.
```
The destination server retries until the lock is released or stale, so items can't exist in two live sessions. (ProfileStore implements this pattern.)

FireServer automatically passes the sending Player as the first argument on the server. The client also passed LocalPlayer explicitly, so the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50): `amount` is the duplicate Player Instance and 50 lands in an unused third parameter, hence arithmetic on an Instance. Fix the client: `remote:FireServer(50)`. And validate on the server, since clients can send anything:
```lua
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount)
	if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount or amount % 1 ~= 0 then return end
	if amount < 0 or amount > 1000 then return end
	print(amount + 1)
end)
```
Never accept a player argument from the client for identity; use the implicit first parameter.
T5:
Race: in Studio solo the local player can join before your server Script runs and connects PlayerAdded (especially if the script yields or requires modules first), so PlayerAdded never fires for that player. On live servers scripts usually finish before anyone joins. Standard fix: connect the handler, then also run it for players already present (guarding against double setup):
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
	if player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats") then return end
	local ls = Instance.new("Folder"); ls.Name = "leaderstats"
	local coins = Instance.new("IntValue"); coins.Name = "Coins"; coins.Parent = ls
	ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Also connect before any yielding work (requires, DataStore loads).

T8: RenderFidelity is being replaced by mesh streaming and cloud LoDs. Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs (Default/Enabled/Disabled; opt-in from April 27, 2026, phase 2 planned to make Default mean Enabled around July 2026): when effectively Enabled, every mesh in the published experience uses the cloud LoD transcoder and mesh streaming, and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored. So meshes drop LoD with distance regardless of Precise, and Studio can differ from live. Check the Workspace property's effective value; Disabled restores the old behaviour only until phase 3 removes the property and RenderFidelity entirely. Real fix: budget triangles and silhouettes at the source so cloud LoDs look good; don't rely on RenderFidelity (pcall any reads, no gameplay logic on it). Collision is unaffected. There are reported bugs of meshes stuck at the lowest LoD; report a repro if a close camera still shows low LoD. (Engine and API Changes 2025-2026.)
